_comment: Scoring vocabulary for BreakingNewsClassifier. Tunable without a rebuild. Matching is affix-tolerant: entries are normalised and light-stemmed the same way headlines are, so 'رئيس' also matches 'الرئيس' and 'وزير' matches 'والوزير'. Multi-word entries are matched as phrases.
_breaking: Explicit breaking markers in the headline or summary. +5 (not cumulative).
_breakingExclusions: Idioms that merely CONTAIN a breaking marker. Removed from the text before breaking keywords are matched. 'حتى الآن' means 'so far' and is ordinary prose — an on-device run had a 7-hour-old wildfire story score the full +5 breaking bonus from it, which is exactly the kind of item this app is supposed to filter out. Without these, 'الآن' is close to useless as a signal.
_breakingPaths: Breaking markers in the URL path, feed name or category. +3.
_politics: Politics seed keywords. First match +2, each further distinct match +1, capped.
_economy: Economy seed keywords. Scored identically to politics.
_topicPaths: Politics/economy sections in the article URL. +2. Deliberately excludes catch-all sections like /news/ — Al Jazeera files literally everything under it, so including it handed +2 to every item that outlet publishes and made the topic threshold meaningless.
_negative: Off-topic vocabulary. Each match subtracts from the topic score, so a sports story cannot ride a stray 'صفقة' or 'هجوم' into the feed.
_negativePaths: Off-topic URL sections. Far more reliable than keywords — CNN files football under /sport/ and Al Jazeera files human-interest under /misc/, neither of which contains a negative keyword in the headline.
_analysisPrefixes: Words that mark an explainer when they OPEN a headline. Position matters: 'لماذا' first is an analysis piece, the same word mid-sentence is ordinary reporting. Paired with the question-mark rule, these catch the format keywords cannot — 'هل يواجه ترامب مأزقا؟' contains no off-topic vocabulary at all.
_eventVerbs: Verbs of occurrence, announcement, decision, force or market movement. REQUIRED for an item to count as breaking (ScoringWeights.requireEventSignal), unless it carries an explicit breaking marker. News is something that happened; a feature is something that is. Listed in the conjugations wire headlines actually use — perfective plus both imperfective persons — because normalisation folds hamza and ta-marbuta but does not conjugate. Includes verbal nouns (masdar) as well as conjugated verbs: Arabic headlines are heavily nominal — «انفجار مقذوفات» is an event containing no verb. Generic nouns that occur in descriptive prose (مواجهة, قرار, دعوة, أزمة, معاناة) are deliberately excluded, because they readmit exactly the features this gate exists to reject. See DECISIONS.md D28.
_religiousEvents: Religious observances and ceremonies. A political figure commenting on a pilgrimage is not breaking political news, and a cleric's name alone was enough to clear the topic bar without these. Deliberately narrow — sectarian *politics* must still get through, so this lists occasions and rites, not institutions or actors.
